evals.prompt: I've just opened an unfamiliar repo that uses several MCP servers and a deploy CLI. Before I start a task that depends on the deploy CLI's dry-run check, work out what's actually available and how far to trust it.
evals.expected_output: Enumerates from live sources (--help, MCP listing, config) rather than docs; classifies capabilities as verified, unverified or absent; checks that the dry-run can actually report a failure using a known-bad fixture (not production) or labels it uncalibrated; reports counts and shapes, not full listings; does not write an inventory file.

evals.prompt: The task needs to update a field on a media channel, and reading the source it looks like no tool exposes it. Should I write a new MCP tool?
evals.expected_output: Proves the gap with a harmless live attempt before building; checks existing tools and compositions first; if building, copies an existing sibling tool's shape; verifies through the real client with a read-back; returns to the task and records any further gap without chasing it.

evals.prompt: It's the start of a normal session on a project I worked on yesterday. Run recon so we know where things stand.
evals.expected_output: Declines a full recon at routine session start and points to the project's /prime (derive state, cite routing facts, cheap pulse check); runs recon only if a pulse check fails or a cited fact proves stale.
